comments.body: This does fix the issue in the test flow I posted, but the change makes decisions on what is in msg.payload and the error is not related to the value in msg.payload.  If the posted flow is changed slightly to Delete msg.payload then again no data are plotted.

> ### Fix
> For a single (non-array) number/string payload, evaluate the configured msg property for y, falling back to the payload if it is undefined. The default (`msg.payload`) is unchanged.

This is the fundamental error here.  It should just read something like:
Where Y is configured as a msg property then use that property for y.

Thanks @colinl, you were right and my first follow-up was incomplete: it only fixed the `_datapoint` computed in `beforeSend`. A message without `msg.payload` (e.g. after `Delete msg.payload`) was still dropped, because `onInput` skipped the history store and the client ignored messages without a payload. Pushed another commit: when Y is a msg property, a message that carries that property now counts as data on the server (stored in history) and on the client (plotted). `ui_update` messages without a payload are still not treated as data. Added tests that check the point reaches the datastore for `{ topic: 'a', value: 3 }`, and that a payload-less `ui_update` does not. I've also updated the description: when Y is a msg property, that property is used for y, with no fallback to the payload.

This comment was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change was tested by running `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js` (the client-side change in `UIChart.vue` has not been exercised in a browser).

The function `addToChart(payload, series)` is a low level functions that adds the data in `payload` to the chart. It should not be testing config or message properties and overriding the passed in `payload` parameter. The fix needs to be at a higher level so that, where a msg property is configured for the Y value, then that is picked up and passed into `addToChart()`

Thanks @colinl, that makes sense. `addToChart` no longer reads the config or the msg: `beforeSend` now resolves the value first (the configured msg property when Y is a msg property, otherwise the payload) and passes it into `addToChart`, which is back to just adding the value it is given. Pushed as a new commit; behaviour and tests are unchanged (`test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js` passes).

This comment was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change was tested by running `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js`.

In the test flow in the issue, if msg.payload is set to an object then addToChart() is called with that object in the first parameter.  Is that intended?  Somehow the correct value does end up getting added to the chart, but not from that parameter.  I do not understand why, if the value to plot is in msg.someProperty, that msg.payload is being tested to see if it is an object.

Also the new function isDataMsg returns true if msg.payload is present.  However, if the value to be charted is coming from, for example, msg.value then the value of msg.payload is irrelevant. If msg.value is not present then it is not a data message whatever the value of msg.payload.

Thanks @colinl. On the first point: you're right that the object case shouldn't be left out. With Y set to a msg property, `beforeSend` now resolves y from that property for object payloads as well, and passes it to `addToChart` instead of letting `addToChart` read the config/msg again. The object payload still supplies x and the series (by key); only y comes from the msg property. Added a test with an object payload and Y = `msg.value`. (The result for objects was already y from the msg property in the plain case, so this is a consistency change, and the test guards it.)

On `isDataMsg`: agreed, it was wrong. When Y is a msg property it no longer looks at `msg.payload`: a msg is data only if that property is present and the msg is not a `ui_update` (an empty-array payload still counts, as the clear request). A msg with a payload but no value in the configured property is not stored. Added a test for that case; `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js` passes.

This comment was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change was tested by running `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js`.

> a msg is data only if that property is present and the msg is not a `ui_update`

It is perfectly valid to have chart data and msg.ui_update in the same message.

> an empty-array payload still counts, as the clear request

I think that possibly, if a message property is specified for the data, then the empty array should be sent to that property rather than msg.payload to clear the chart.  What do you think?
@n-lark I think your opinion is needed here.

Thanks @colinl. Agreed on `ui_update`: it can travel with chart data, so I removed that exclusion. When Y is a msg property, a msg is now data whenever that property is present, with or without `msg.ui_update`; a `ui_update` msg without it is still not stored. Added a test for the combined case, which fails without the change.

On clearing: sending the empty array to the configured property (e.g. `msg.value = []`) does seem more consistent with taking the data from there. The catch is compatibility: `msg.payload = []` clears the chart today, including for charts where Y is already a msg property other than `payload`, so existing flows could rely on it. The options I see are (a) keep `msg.payload = []` only, (b) accept `[]` in either place, or (c) move to the configured property only. I'd lean towards (b), but have not changed this behaviour and will follow what you and @n-lark prefer.

This comment was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change was tested by running `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js`.

Why does isDataMsg() always return true if msg.payload is an array, even if msg.payload is not the source of the data t be plotted?
Similarly line 144
`                const yFromMsg = config.yAxisPropertyType === 'msg' && !Array.isArray(p) && isDataMsg(msg)`
is affected by msg.payload being an array for some reason.

I am having difficulty working out why the new override parameter is necessary in addToChart, can you explain the logic please?
Another issue. If Y is set to msg.value.y then ui_update messages do not appear to be getting through to the chart.  It is ok if Y is msg.value.

Thanks, Colin. The array exception in `isDataMsg()` was there to preserve the existing clear command. It was too broad, so it now applies only to `msg.payload = []`. With Y set to `msg.value`, that still clears the chart and its history even when `msg.value` is absent. A non-empty payload array without `msg.value` is ignored. The clear command still uses `msg.payload` while you and @n-lark consider the API.

The override was intended to let an object payload supply X and series while getting Y from the configured message property. The object path already reads that property, so the override was redundant and has been removed. The array path already processes the payload separately, which also makes the explicit array check in `yFromMsg` redundant.

For `msg.value.y`, Node-RED throws when the parent property is missing. The server now treats that missing path as absent chart data and still sends the options update to the client. The widget tests cover the socket update and the empty-payload clear command, and all 11 pass.

This reply was drafted with AI assistance.

Thanks @colinl. The JSON-series flow plotted nothing because the new data check required a value at the Y property (`payload.value` in your flow), even though the editor hides that field when Series is JSON and the series keys supply the values. The Y property is now ignored for JSON series, and also for histograms, where the field is hidden too. Each case now has a test in `test/nodes/widgets/ui_chart.spec.js` (both fail without the change). Your flow has not been tried in a browser yet.
